finding.claim: validateRealm only applies its private/loopback/link-local IP check when the realm host is an IP literal, so a bearer realm given as a hostname that resolves to a private or metadata address (e.g. 169.254.169.254, 10.x) is accepted. The client then sends a GET or POST to that internal address. Severity low, confidence plausible: the response is mostly blind, and error bodies are echoed only as structured JSON errors.
finding.source: WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="..." header in a 401 response from a registry the user chose to contact (attacker = registry operator). Parsed in registry/remote/auth/challenge.go:67-132 (parseChallenge).
finding.sink: Outbound HTTP request to the realm URL in registry/remote/auth/client.go:417-434 (fetchDistributionToken GET) and 488-494 (fetchOAuth2Token POST), reached through c.send at client.go:136-159.

trace.note: parseChallenge extracts realm param from attacker-controlled header
scheme check: https always allowed, http only if registry is not https
IP-literal-only private-range check; hostnames skip it
Basic auth attached if stored credentials exist
response read with 8 KiB limit; only JSON errors array returned to caller

finding.guards_checked: Scheme restriction (https or http-only-if-registry-http) at client.go:225-234: holds. IP-literal loopback/link-local/private/unspecified check at client.go:235-241: bypassed by hostname. Cross-origin redirect Authorization stripping at client.go:149-152: does not apply, since realm is requested directly. Origin check on challenge at client.go:304: passes, since the challenge came from the registry itself. Response size limits and errutil error echo at errutil.go:43: limit exfiltration to structured JSON errors. Cross-host realm with credentials (client.go:356-363): documented design, not reported.
